22.21.2.en: When we hear the commandment from the mouth of a servant of God, or read it in the Holy Bible, or hear it from the mouth of a friend or from a book, we truly sense a personal relationship with God, as though He were speaking to us directly. We hear His divine voice within us, and our depths respond to His love, for there is no place fitting for the divine Word like the heart, because it is the treasury of love and the temple of the Holy Spirit.

22.21.3.en: Pope Gregory (the Great) sees that what Eliphaz uttered, though it represents sincere counsel, was mistaken in that he supposed himself to be righteous, more righteous than the wicked Job, as he thought, and so took the position of a teacher, a wise man and a proud leader. He represents the heretics of all ages who make light of the Church of God and accuse her of ignorance together with evil, and who want to present her with teachings as righteous teachers, possessors of understanding and knowledge and bearers of righteousness!

22.21.4.en: * There is a sin in a man's teaching someone better than himself, the crime that heretics often commit, teaching while they hold mistaken concepts... This applies also to such persons, as he adds: [I ask you to receive the law from his mouth], for they imagine that what they think out of their own minds comes from the mouth of God.

22.22.s.en: 12. Repentance is a return to the Almighty

22.22.0.en: "If thou return to the Almighty, thou shalt be built up,

22.22.1.en: thou shalt put away iniquity far from thy tabernacles" [23].

22.22.2.en: Eliphaz presents a correct, positive and effective understanding of repentance. Repentance is not merely turning back from sin, for this negative side does not satisfy the soul, but its positive side is that it is a return to the Almighty, and this satisfies the depths and builds them up. For the Almighty alone, by His Holy Spirit, can renew the heart continually without interruption, until it is formed to become truly the icon of God.

22.22.3.en: When man draws near to the divine light he does not allow darkness, especially injustice, to creep into him, because there is no fellowship between light and darkness. Therefore Eliphaz says: [If you put away iniquity from your tabernacle]. Here he refers to the tent of the family or household as a whole, just as the tent refers to the body in which the soul dwells as in a tent.

22.22.4.en: Pope Gregory (the Great) sees that Eliphaz had learned some true things from his friend Job, but he had deviations from the straight line, or from the truth. So we find in the heretics some true concepts that they learned from the Church of Christ, but they mixed what is evangelical truth with the falsehood of their own.

22.22.5.en: * Since Eliphaz was the friend of a blessed person, he perceives some things truly, but on some points he left the straight line and became like the heretics. Therefore he did not realize that Job had been struck with trials because of good qualities. He thought that this man whom he saw stricken had sinned, and so he promised him that if he returned to Almighty God iniquity would be removed from his tent.

22.23.s.en: 13. Repentance is the way of riches

22.23.0.en: 24 "Then shalt thou lay up gold as dust, and the gold of Ophir as the stones of the brooks. 25 Yea, the Almighty shall be thy gold, and thou shalt have plenty of silver" [24].

22.23.1.en: Eliphaz sees that when man cleaves to God, the source of good things, he becomes very rich, so that gold nuggets become for him as plentiful as dust, or gold is laid up with him like dust, and he has much silver.

22.23.2.en: Eliphaz imagined that Job had gathered his wealth by injustice and therefore lost it, but if he cleaves to God, He will give him good things and riches that he will not lose. Perhaps he did not refer here to wealth in livestock and land, but to gold and silver, because what he obtained before was the wealth of farmers and shepherds, whereas what he will obtain by his cleaving to the Lord is the wealth of kings, in gold and silver.

22.23.3.en: With the abundance of gold nuggets and the gold of Ophir, he does not put these treasures in storehouses under strict guard, because he does not fear losing them, nor does he put them in his bosom, because they do not occupy his heart, but sees them as dust and pebbles that do not occupy his thought and heart.

22.23.4.en: This can be interpreted spiritually: whoever returns to God casts gold nuggets on the dust, because he possesses God and so counts everything as refuse for His sake, and he casts pure gold among the stones of the brooks, since gold is not valuable in his eyes but is like the little stones and pebbles that fill the valleys, worth nothing.

22.24.0.en: "Yea, the Almighty shall be thy gold, and thou shalt have plenty of silver" [25].

22.24.1.en: When the righteous cast the gold nuggets of this world into the dust and its gold of Ophir into the brooks among the stones, they find God to be their nuggets and their heavenly gold. He becomes their treasure which will not be stolen from them.

22.24.2.en: Silver in the Holy Bible often refers to the word of God, therefore it is fitting for believers to acquire this spiritual silver, which gives them surpassing spiritual riches, and strength against the coming enemy of good, and inner joy and exultation, so that they share the heavenly beings in their praises. By the divine Word the believer becomes rich, a good soldier of the Lord Christ and a psalmist full of joy.

22.24.3.en: And as the people of the world delight in their wealth, but only for a time, the righteous are glad in God, their true treasure, wealth, honor and strength forever. [The LORD is my strength and song] (Ex 15:2; Ps 118:14; Isa 12:2).

22.24.4.en: Whoever possesses silver in his heart pleads with the word of God and is fortified against the powers of darkness, but if he submits to evil and to the powers of darkness and surrenders to them, he does not perceive the mysteries of God which the divine Word proclaims.

22.24.5.en: * What other enemies do we submit to more than the evil spirits, who besiege us in our thoughts, storm the city of our minds and gain control of it, and take us captive under the yoke of their authority?

22.24.6.en: The Psalmist testifies that the name "silver" refers to divine inspiration, as he says: [The words of the LORD are pure words: as silver tried in a furnace of earth, purified seven times] (Ps 12:6).

22.24.7.en: Often our souls do not enjoy divine inspiration when we submit in a dangerous way to the deceptions of the evil spirits, who sprinkle on our minds the dust of earthly thoughts so that our inner eyes grow dark and do not enjoy the light of inner vision. This is what the Psalmist suffered when he said: [Depart from me, ye evildoers: for I will keep the commandments of my God] (Ps 119:15), teaching us clearly that he could not search into God's commandments when he was suffering in his mind from the snares of the evil spirits.

22.24.9.en: In the parable of the son who returned to his father, the Lord Christ revealed the riches that we enjoy through repentance, for we delight in the greatest position, namely adoption by God, by which He does not hold back from offering us the best robe, the ring of sonship and the shoes, that we may walk in the way of truth in safety and bear witness to God's tender fatherhood.

22.24.10.en: * He brings you the robe, the ring and the shoes.

22.24.11.en: The robe is the garment of wisdom with which the Apostles covered the nakedness of their bodies, and with which every man is clothed. They took the robe in order to cover the weaknesses of their bodies with the power of spiritual wisdom, and of wisdom it was said: "he washed his garments in wine" (Gen 49:11). The robe is the spiritual clothing and the wedding garment.

22.24.12.en: The ring is nothing other than the deed of true faith and the seal of truth.

22.24.13.en: The shoes refer to the preaching of the Gospel.

22.24.14.en: St. Ambrose * The best robe is the honor that Adam lost, and the servants who brought it are the preachers of reconciliation... The ring on the hand is the earnest of the Holy Spirit because of the fellowship of grace, for the Spirit is rightly indicated by the finger...

22.24.15.en: The shoes on the feet are the readiness to preach the Gospel, that we may not touch earthly things.

22.25.s.en: 14. By repentance the face is lifted up to God

22.25.0.en: "For then shalt thou have thy delight in the Almighty, and shalt lift up thy face unto God" [26].

22.25.1.en: The righteous man enjoys boldness before God: "thou shalt lift up thy face unto God," so that he is not terrified and his heart is not broken, but with gladness of heart and confidence he appears before God, speaks with Him and seeks a life of fellowship with Him.

22.25.2.en: Pope Gregory (the Great) sees that Eliphaz spoke the truth if this speech were directed to a wicked man unable to lift his inner face toward God. But he erred, because he presented what is true without wisdom, presenting it in order to direct an accusation against righteous Job.

22.25.3.en: People know us by looking at our faces, and so they distinguish us from one another. One who does not lift up his face before people and appear before them is not known by them. So when man returns by repentance to God, he finds his delight in Almighty God and lifts his inner face to God, and so becomes known to Him and not a stranger to Him. Therefore in every Divine Liturgy the priest cries out: "Lift up your hearts," or "Where are your hearts?" and by the power of the Spirit the people answer: "We have them with the Lord." It is as though they were declaring that their inner faces are lifted up to the Lord, who is pleased with them, and that union with Him gives them awe.

22.25.4.en: * Lifting up the face to God is lifting up the heart, searching for what is highest of all. Just as by the bodily face we are known and distinguished among men, so by the inner form we are known before God. But when we are weighed down with the iniquity of sin and sink to the earth, we fear to lift up the face of our heart to God, since we do not stand with any confidence in good works. The mind is filled with fear as to looking toward the heavenly things, because conscience itself accuses it. But by the tears of repentance sin is washed away, and man laments the things that were committed so that he no longer commits what he laments, and so we enjoy confidence in the mind, and the face of our heart is lifted up to contemplate the delights of the reward.

22.25.5.en: Eliphaz is reckoned to have spoken the truth, if he were counseling a weak person, but when he looks with contempt upon a righteous man because of his blows, what is this but pouring out words of knowledge without knowledge?

22.26.s.en: 15. Repentance opens the gates of heaven

22.26.0.en: 27 "Thou shalt make thy prayer unto him, and he shall hear thee, and thou shalt pay thy vows. 28 Thou shalt also decree a thing, and it shall be established unto thee: and the light shall shine upon thy ways."

22.26.1.en: "Thou shalt make thy prayer unto him, and he shall hear thee, and thou shalt pay thy vows" [27].

22.26.2.en: When Eliphaz calls Job to repent of his evils and return to God, he assures him that through his repentance he will pray to God and He will answer him.

22.26.3.en: This is true speech, for repentance opens the gates of heaven and gives us boldness before God, and God inclines His ear to hear us, and our prayers smell like the fragrance of good incense rising before Him.

22.26.4.en: The penitent enters into a dialogue of love with God, and finds himself before the throne of grace, and offers his vows as a response to God's answering of his prayers. He offers vows of thanksgiving and praise.

22.26.5.en: What Eliphaz aimed at by these words, which no blemish touches except Eliphaz's evil intention, was to accuse Job of not being a man of God. The prayers that he offered to God all the days of his life were not accepted, because they came from an unrepentant heart and a soul that does not return to God, and his vows he will not pay even if he offered sacrifices for his children to this extent and gave countless offerings, because his heart is not pure.

22.26.6.en: What his words carried of divine truth, which suits every soul to return to God, Eliphaz used as a sword with which to strike the soul of righteous Job to shatter him and bring him into the hell of despair.

22.26.7.en: * As for those who count the Lord's commandments as nothing, they offer prayers and the Lord never hears them. Therefore it is written: [He that turneth away his ear from hearing the law, even his prayer shall be abomination] (Prov 28:9). Since Eliphaz believes that blessed Job was not heard, he insists that he has practiced some wrong.

22.26.9.en: * Repentance is a fire that consumes all human weakness, removes negligence, laziness and the heaviness of the body, and gives the soul a wing with which it flies toward heaven, and shows it, from this high summit, the vanity of this present life.

22.26.10.en: One who does not rise to the observation post cannot take a true picture of the earth and its contents. For many things darken the field of vision, deafen the ears and make the tongue stammer. Therefore it is fitting for man to wrest himself from this clamor, to keep away from the smoke, and to enter into solitude, to find deep peace, calm and stillness with enlightenment.

22.26.11.en: When the eyes are fixed on the love of God, and the ear no longer hears anything but His words as though they were a sweet spiritual symphony, the soul becomes a captive (of God) and feels disgust for food and sleep.

22.26.12.en: It is true that the noise of the world and material concerns glide over the soul, but they do not enter it, and with the soul's rising in this way it no longer cares about the crackling of earthly storms.

22.26.13.en: And as the dwellers on the mountains no longer hear the sounds of the city nor see what goes on in it, but count all this like an indistinct din, so those who have left the world of their own will and set out flying in the heights of philosophy (wisdom) no longer perceive anything of the world's affairs, because all their senses are directed toward heaven.

22.26.14.en: Therefore let us seek not only the solitude of the wilderness but the solitude of inner desire. Let us hide on the highest summit of the soul, where nothing earthly dwells.

22.26.15.en: The power of repentance is like a wind that drives away dust and sweeps away passions faster than smoke.

22.27.0.en: St. John Chrysostom "Thou shalt also decree a thing, and it shall be established unto thee: and the light shall shine upon thy ways" [28].

22.27.1.en: The penitent man finds inner rest in the management of all his outward affairs: "Thou shalt also decree a thing, and it shall be established unto thee." And as it was said of the righteous man who walks in the law of the Lord: "whatsoever he doeth shall prosper" (Ps 1:3).

22.27.2.en: "The light shall shine upon thy ways," that is, God will guide you. For whoever returns to the Lord by repentance finds the word of God a lamp that lights the way for him, as the Word brings him into the Kingdom of light.

22.28.0.en: "When men are cast down, then thou shalt say, There is lifting up;

22.28.1.en: and he shall save the humble person" [29].

22.28.2.en: The Jesuit translation has: "and to him who humbles himself you will say: Rise up," when despair tries to creep into the hearts and thoughts of the penitent and almost swallows them, they find the grace of God within them strengthening them, that they may enjoy the sublime, successful life: [I will cause thee to ride upon the high places of the earth] (Isa 58:14). True repentance gives true humility, as it gives man a return to God, who lifts up the humble.

22.28.3.en: Sadly, what Eliphaz means here is not to offer counsel to every man to enjoy true humility, but to assert that the complete collapse to which Job had come, so that his place was on the dunghill, was merely the fruit of his pride and arrogance even before God, so that he prepared himself for destruction.

22.28.4.en: * "For he who is humbled will be glorified, and he who lowers his eyes will be saved" [29]. This phrase does not contradict the mouth of truth, who said: "for every one that exalteth himself shall be abased; and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted" (Lk 14:11). So it was said of Solomon: "Before destruction the heart of man is haughty, and before honour is humility" (Prov 18:12).

22.28.5.en: Fittingly it was said: "he who lowers his eyes will be saved," because pride is discovered through the service of the members, for its first announcement usually appears in the eyes. It is written: "thou wilt bring down high looks" (Ps 18:27)... So "lowering the eyes" does not mean that a man looks downward, but that he reckons himself less and beneath all that is visible.

22.28.7.en: * It is more fitting (for the sick man to tell his physician), confessing the faults into which he fell, than to keep his wounds hidden and to be fanatical, boasting and exposing the wounds of others. It is no wonder that the tax collector went away healed, since he was not ashamed to show the place of his pain.

22.28.8.en: St. Augustine * Where will you be when the demons come near you? For humility brings them down from their rank.

22.28.9.en: When they see you humble they flee from you.

22.28.10.en: Humility is the house of divinity, and where it is, God dwells in it.

22.28.11.en: Look: in whom do I dwell but in the meek, the humble, who fears my words?

22.28.12.en: Let your soul be humbled, and the King will come and dwell in you, and the whole power of the enemy will not overcome you.

22.28.13.en: For the house of the King is not robbed by thieves, because His soldiers guard its doors carefully.

22.28.14.en: If you are humble He will dwell in you in that kingdom, and thieves will not rob you.

22.28.15.en: If you humble yourself you will uproot the tree of evil, and plant in its place the blessed tree of our Lord.

22.28.16.en: If love of His divinity is kindled in you, it makes you deaf, and all the evils (that come upon you) will be as good things.

22.28.17.en: You look upon insult and mockery and all bitter abuse as though they were good things and not evils...

22.29.s.en: 17. By repentance we intercede for our brethren

22.29.0.en: "He delivereth him that is not innocent: and it is delivered by the pureness of thine hands" [30].

22.29.1.en: Eliphaz ended his speech by directing a harsh rebuke to Job. For if Job had been accustomed to offer sacrifices for his children, in case they had sinned even in thought against God (Job 1:5), reckoning himself and the members of his household more righteous than others, then God did not hear him, and did not deliver him or rescue his children, and this is a sign of his wickedness. The man who returns to God asks even for others who are not innocent, and He delivers them, for the sake of the cleanness of the hands of the righteous man who lifts his hands in prayer. It is as though he were making light of Job, saying to him: If your hands were clean your prayers and your sacrifices for yourself and your family would have been accepted, but because they are evil they have brought evil upon all!

22.29.2.en: Truly the godly man does not enjoy God's work in him alone, but as he prays for others with a wide heart God answers him, as the Apostle Paul did when he was in the ship (Acts 27:24).

22.29.3.en: Eliphaz did not realize that what he said would actually be fulfilled, when Job prayed for him and for his two companions (Job 42:8).

22.29.4.en: Perhaps Eliphaz prophesies, without knowing it, about the Lord Christ, the Intercessor and Atoning One. Who is this one with clean hands but the Lord Christ, who alone is without sin?

22.29.5.en: He stretched out His hands on the Cross, asking: "My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?" He rose by His power, granting guilty humanity the possibility of salvation and victory over death, and deliverance!

22.29.6.en: Truly our Christ alone, by His blood, delivers the man who is not innocent, by the power of His blood shed on the Cross.

22.29.7.en: Let me return to You by repentance,
